sections.h2: Where does the Williamson County Register of Deeds record a deed?
sections.html:
The Williamson County Register of Deeds is at 1320 West Main Street, Suite 201, in Franklin, TN 37064. The mailing address is P. O. Box 808, Franklin, TN 37065, the phone number is 615-790-5706, and the office takes questions at register@williamsoncounty-tn.gov. Counter hours run Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, and the elected Register is Sherry Anderson.

The office keeps the public record of deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, plats, liens, judgments, wills and similar instruments. Its own site ties that duty to T.C.A. 66-24-101. A deed that never reaches this office stays invisible to a title search, so the recording step matters even on a quick sale.

Several other county desks sit in the same building on West Main Street. The County Clerk is in Suite 135, the Trustee in Suite 203 and the Property Assessor in Suite 300, which makes it simple to settle a records question and a tax question on one trip.

sections.h2: What is Williamson County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Williamson County is a Middle Tennessee county of about 584 square miles, created by the General Assembly on October 26, 1799 from part of Davidson County. Franklin is the county seat and the largest city, and the county also holds Brentwood, Fairview, Spring Hill (partly in Maury County), Nolensville and Thompson's Station. The Harpeth River and the Little Harpeth River are the main streams.

The county counted 247,726 residents in the 2020 census and an estimated 272,061 in 2025, up from 183,182 in 2010. That census count included 91,133 housing units, and 78.5% of occupied homes were owner occupied. Williamson County Schools operates 50 schools, with a slice of Franklin served by the Franklin Special School District for grades K to 8.

Growth has been steady since the interstate era tied the county to Nashville, so most sales here involve a recorded deed of trust being released and a new one being filed. The Register's office handles both sides of that paperwork.

sections.h2: Which recordation taxes apply to a Williamson County deed?
sections.html:
Tennessee charges two recordation taxes, and the Register of Deeds collects them at filing and remits them to the Department of Revenue. The realty transfer tax is owed by the grantee on a transfer of real property. The indebtedness tax applies to a recorded deed of trust or mortgage.

Tennessee recordation taxes collected at the Williamson County Register of Deeds
TaxRateApplies to
Realty transfer tax37 cents per $100, generally on the greater of price paid or property valueDeeds and other transfer instruments
Indebtedness (mortgage) tax$0.115 per $100 of debt, after the first $2,000Deeds of trust, mortgages, financing statements

Source: Tennessee Department of Revenue, recordation tax overview, citing Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409.

As arithmetic, a $500,000 purchase carries $1,850 in transfer tax at 37 cents per $100. A $400,000 loan carries $457.70 in indebtedness tax, since the first $2,000 is excluded. Your closing agent will show the exact lines on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What recording fees does the Williamson County office charge?
sections.html:
The office posts a fee calculator on its ProAccess system. You choose the instrument type, enter the page count, and the screen returns a recording fee, a register's fee, a DP fee and an archive fee, followed by a total due. Using the calculator is better than guessing, because the total moves with the number of pages.

The instrument list is long. It includes deed, quitclaim deed, trustee's deed, installment deed, deed of trust, release, plat, easement, lis pendens, power of attorney and last will and testament. Most home sales touch three of those: the warranty or quitclaim deed, the release of the seller's old deed of trust, and the buyer's new deed of trust.

Fees for the same instrument can change when the county or state adjusts them, so rely on the calculator for the day you file. Ask the Register's staff at 615-790-5706 if a document type is unusual.

sections.h2: How can I file documents with the Williamson County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
You can file at the counter in Franklin or send documents through an electronic recording partner. The office lists four approved e-recording services on its site.

  • CSC (cscglobal.com)
  • ERecording Partners Network (goepn.com)
  • Indecomm Global Services (indecomm.com)
  • Simplifile (simplifile.com)

Title companies and lenders normally submit through one of these channels. A private seller closing without a title company can still bring the signed, notarized deed to the counter, along with payment for the fee total and the transfer tax.

The office also publishes a fraud alert subscription, TitleSearcher for searching records, and Pro Access for professional account holders. If you want to know whether anyone has recorded something against your parcel, a name search on those tools is a good habit before listing.

sections.h2: Which release and correction forms does the office provide?
sections.html:
The office posts downloadable forms for the documents sellers most often need after a payoff. Using the county's own version keeps the filing format right.

  • Notice of Completion
  • Release of Judgment
  • Release of Lien
  • Release of Trust Deed
  • Request for redaction of a Social Security number or military discharge information

A release of trust deed is the document that clears your old mortgage from the record after payoff. If a lender never recorded one, a clean title search will show it, and your title agent can chase it before the sale date. The redaction forms help owners whose Social Security number or military discharge papers sit in a public image.

sections.h2: How do Williamson County property taxes interact with a sale?
sections.html:
Williamson County tax bills are mailed in early October and are payable from the first Monday in October through February 28 of the following year. Partial payments are accepted. On March 1, interest begins at 1.5%, accruing the first of each month, and the Trustee has no authority to waive, prorate or release any piece of the tax or interest.

The tax year covers January 1 through December 31, and bills go to the owner of record as of January 1. If you sell, you must forward the bill to the new owner, and the contract or the title company normally sets who covers what share at closing. The Trustee is at 1320 West Main Street, Suite 203, phone 615-790-5709. The Assessor handles value questions at 615-790-5708.

For an unpaid bill, ask the Trustee for the amount due on your parcel before the contract date. That figure lets the closing agent pay the county from your proceeds in one step.

sections.h2: What should I do before a Williamson County deed is recorded?
sections.html:
A short checklist prevents most recording delays. Gather these items first and confirm them with your closing agent.

  • Order a title search so liens and old deeds of trust surface early.
  • Confirm the Trustee has no balance on the parcel for the current tax year.
  • Have every signature notarized with the notary block filled in completely.
  • Run the fee calculator with the real page count so the check or wire amount is right.
  • Decide whether the closing will file in person or through one of the four e-recording partners.

After recording, the office stamps the instrument with its book and page reference. Keep the recorded copy with your closing file, because lenders and buyers ask for it years later.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Williamson County sale?
faqs.a: The grantee, meaning the buyer, owes the realty transfer tax under Tennessee's recordation tax rules. The rate is 37 cents per $100, generally measured on the greater of the price or the property's value. Contracts sometimes shift the cost, so check your sales agreement.

faqs.q: What are the Williamson County Register of Deeds office hours?
faqs.a: The counter is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM at 1320 West Main Street, Suite 201, Franklin. Call 615-790-5706 to confirm hours around holidays. Electronic recording partners accept submissions outside counter hours.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed in Williamson County without a title company?
faqs.a: Yes. You can bring a signed, notarized deed to the Register's office and pay the fees shown on the calculator plus the transfer tax. A title search beforehand still helps, since it exposes liens that would follow the property.

faqs.q: Does the Register of Deeds collect property taxes?
faqs.a: No. Property taxes are paid to the Williamson County Trustee at Suite 203 of the same building, phone 615-790-5709. The Register only collects the recordation taxes and recording fees that apply when an instrument is filed.

faqs.q: What happens to my property tax bill if I sell in Williamson County?
faqs.a: Bills go to the owner of record as of January 1, and the seller must pass the bill to the new owner. The county will not prorate or waive interest, so the contract and closing statement decide the split. Ask the Trustee for the balance before closing.
